title: Matthew Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 23.

questions.question: In Matthew 23, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat
He that is greatest among you shall be your servant
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees
questions.explanation: This is the first thing mentioned in the chapter where Jesus addresses the multitude and His disciples.

questions.question: According to Matthew 23, who sits in Moses' seat?
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Matthew 23:2, where it mentions the scribes and Pharisees sitting in Moses' seat.

questions.question: What should people observe and do according to Matthew 23?
options: What the scribes and Pharisees bid them
questions.correctAnswer: What the scribes and Pharisees bid them
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:3 states that people should observe and do whatever the scribes and Pharisees bid them.

questions.question: What do the scribes and Pharisees bind on men's shoulders?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:4 mentions that they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne on men's shoulders.

questions.question: Why do the scribes and Pharisees do their works?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:5 states that all their works they do for to be seen of men.

questions.question: What do the scribes and Pharisees love at feasts?
questions.explanation: According to Matthew 23:6, they love the uppermost rooms at feasts.

questions.question: What title do the scribes and Pharisees desire in the markets?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 23:7, it states they desire to be called Rabbi in the markets.

questions.question: Who is the Master according to Matthew 23?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:8 indicates that one is your Master, even Christ.

questions.question: What should people not call any man on earth?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:9 states that people should not call any man their father upon the earth.

questions.question: What is said about the one who is greatest among you?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:11 states that he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.

questions.question: What happens to the one who exalts himself according to Matthew 23?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 23:12, it is stated that whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus spoke to the multitude and his disciples in Matthew 23.
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in Matthew 23:1 where it states that Jesus spoke to the multitude and his disciples.

questions.question: True or False: The scribes and Pharisees are mentioned as hypocrites in Matthew 23.
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:13 refers to the scribes and Pharisees as hypocrites.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus called for the scribes and Pharisees to be honored in public.
questions.explanation: The text does not say that Jesus called for the scribes and Pharisees to be honored in public; rather, it criticizes their behavior.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus instructed his disciples to follow the ways of the Pharisees.
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:3 indicates that while the disciples should observe what the Pharisees bid, they should not follow their works.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What do the scribes and Pharisees do to widows' houses?
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in Matthew 23:14 where it says, 'for ye devour widows' houses...'

questions.question: What does Matthew 23:14 promise will happen to those who devour widows' houses?
options: They shall receive the greater damnation
questions.correctAnswer: They shall receive the greater damnation
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:14 states, 'therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.'

questions.question: What is the fate of a proselyte made by the scribes and Pharisees according to Matthew 23:15?
options: He becomes twofold more the child of hell
questions.correctAnswer: He becomes twofold more the child of hell
questions.explanation: This is affirmed in Matthew 23:15 where it says, 'ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.'

questions.question: What do the scribes and Pharisees say about swearing by the temple according to Matthew 23:16?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:16 states, 'Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing.'

questions.question: According to Matthew 23:23, what weightier matters have the scribes and Pharisees omitted?
questions.explanation: This is specified in Matthew 23:23, which mentions the omission of 'judgment, mercy, and faith.'

questions.question: What does Matthew 23:24 indicate about the scribes and Pharisees' focus?
options: They strain at a gnat and swallow a camel
They are wise in their understanding
questions.correctAnswer: They strain at a gnat and swallow a camel
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:24 illustrates that they focus on minor issues while neglecting more significant ones.

questions.question: What does Matthew 23:25 say about the inner condition of the cup and platter?
options: They are full of extortion and excess
questions.correctAnswer: They are full of extortion and excess
questions.explanation: In Matthew 23:25, it states, 'but within they are full of extortion and excess.'

questions.question: What must the blind Pharisee cleanse first, according to Matthew 23:26?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:26 instructs, 'cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter.'

questions.question: What is the relationship between humility and greatness according to Matthew 23:12?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:12 states, 'he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.'

questions.question: What does Matthew 23:4 say about the burdens placed by the scribes and Pharisees?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 23:4, it mentions, 'For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne...'

questions.question: What title does Jesus caution against using in Matthew 23:8?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:8 warns, 'But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ.'

questions.question: According to Matthew 23:3, what should people do regarding the teachings of the scribes and Pharisees?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:3 advises to 'observe, and do; but do not ye after their works.'

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus spoke to both the multitude and his disciples in Matthew 23?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:1 states, 'Then spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples.'

questions.question: Is it false that the Pharisees do not burden others according to Matthew 23:4?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:4 reveals they 'bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne.'

questions.question: Is it false that the scribes and Pharisees are called hypocrites in Matthew 23?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:13 starts with 'But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!' confirming they are called hypocrites.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 23.

questions.question: What analogy does Jesus use to describe the scribes and Pharisees in Matthew 23:27?
questions.explanation: Jesus compares the scribes and Pharisees to whited sepulchres in Matthew 23:27, emphasizing their outward appearance of beauty while being inwardly corrupt.

questions.question: According to Matthew 23:28, how do the scribes and Pharisees appear to men?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:28 states that the scribes and Pharisees outwardly appear righteous to men, highlighting their hypocrisy.

questions.question: What do the scribes and Pharisees say about their ancestors' actions in Matthew 23:30?
options: They would not kill the prophets
They would have supported the prophets
They would have stoned the prophets
They would have ignored the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: They would not kill the prophets
questions.explanation: In Matthew 23:30, the scribes and Pharisees claim that had they lived in the days of their ancestors, they would not have participated in the killing of the prophets.

questions.question: What does Jesus call the scribes and Pharisees in Matthew 23:33?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 23:33, Jesus addresses the scribes and Pharisees as 'serpents' and 'generation of vipers,' indicating their deceitfulness.

questions.question: What will happen to the generation of the scribes and Pharisees according to Matthew 23:36?
options: All these things shall come upon this generation
questions.correctAnswer: All these things shall come upon this generation
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:36 indicates that Jesus prophesies dire consequences for the current generation of the scribes and Pharisees.

questions.question: What does Jesus express a desire to do for Jerusalem in Matthew 23:37?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:37 shows Jesus lamenting over Jerusalem, expressing a desire to gather its children together as a hen gathers her chicks.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'hypokrites' in Matthew 23:27 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Hypokrites' in Greek means 'actor' or 'one who wears a mask,' referring to those who pretend to be what they are not, as the Pharisees did.

questions.question: Which literary device is employed when Jesus uses the term 'whited sepulchres' in Matthew 23:27?
questions.explanation: The term 'whited sepulchres' is a metaphor illustrating the contrast between outward beauty and inward corruption.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the theme of hypocrisy found in Matthew 23:28?
questions.explanation: James 1:22 emphasizes not just hearing the word but doing it, paralleling the theme of hypocrisy found in Matthew 23:28.

questions.question: What does Matthew 23:34 foreshadow about the treatment of Jesus' followers?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:34 foreshadows the persecution of Jesus' followers, as He sends prophets and wise men whom they will persecute.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Matthew 23:36?
options: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees
All these things shall come upon this generation
Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers
questions.correctAnswer: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:35 concludes the thought about the bloodshed and is followed by the declaration of judgment in verse 36.

questions.question: Which verse provides a contrast to the Pharisees' attitude of outward righteousness found in Matthew 23:28?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:13 highlights that the people honor God with their lips but their hearts are far from Him, echoing the hypocrisy in Matthew 23:28.

questions.question: The statement 'your house is left unto you desolate' in Matthew 23:38 is an indication of what?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:38 indicates judgment upon Jerusalem, signifying that God’s presence has left due to their rejection of the prophets.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus expresses a desire to gather the children of Jerusalem together in Matthew 23:37.
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:37 shows Jesus lamenting over Jerusalem and expressing a desire to gather its children, indicating His compassion.

questions.question: True or False: The scribes and Pharisees are praised for their outward righteousness in Matthew 23:28.
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:28 indicates that while they appear righteous outwardly, they are full of hypocrisy and iniquity, not praised.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 23:3 teach about human sin and religious hypocrisy?
options: Religious leaders may command rightly but fail in their own obedience
Religious leaders are exempt from judgment because of their office
True righteousness is only external and visible
Religious laws are burdensome and to be avoided
questions.correctAnswer: Religious leaders may command rightly but fail in their own obedience
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:3 states that the scribes and Pharisees 'say, and do not,' indicating a failure in obedience despite correct teaching, highlighting the sin of hypocrisy.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's judgment is taught in Matthew 23:15 regarding proselytes?
options: False converts can be more severely judged than their teachers
All proselytes are saved regardless of their conduct
Proselytizing guarantees entrance into the kingdom
Judgment is based solely on ethnic lineage
questions.correctAnswer: False converts can be more severely judged than their teachers
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:15 warns that making a proselyte who becomes 'twofold more the child of hell' teaches the doctrine that false converts can face harsher judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's priorities in obedience is taught in Matthew 23:23?
options: God values justice, mercy, and faithfulness over meticulous tithing
Tithing of small herbs is more important than moral obedience
Religious rituals are the highest form of worship
Faith alone without works is sufficient
questions.correctAnswer: God values justice, mercy, and faithfulness over meticulous tithing
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:23 highlights that while tithing is commanded, the 'weightier matters' of judgment, mercy, and faith are not to be neglected, teaching God's priority on justice and mercy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 23:37 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:37 shows Jesus lamenting over Jerusalem's rejection despite His repeated desire to gather them, demonstrating God's longsuffering patience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Matthew 23:22 through the reference to swearing by heaven?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:22's reference to swearing by heaven as the throne of God reveals God's sovereign rule over all creation.

questions.question: How does Matthew 23 prepare the theme of prophetic rejection and judgment found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: By condemning the religious leaders for killing prophets and predicting judgment on this generation
By affirming that all leaders are righteous and will be saved
By teaching that the temple will be rebuilt and glorified
By focusing solely on individual salvation apart from community
questions.correctAnswer: By condemning the religious leaders for killing prophets and predicting judgment on this generation
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:34-36 connects to the broader biblical theme of prophetic rejection and judgment, highlighting Israel's history and impending judgment on Jesus' contemporaries.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Matthew 23:39 make regarding the coming of the Messiah?
options: The Messiah will return only when Israel acknowledges Him as blessed
The Messiah will return regardless of Israel's response
The Messiah's coming ends the Old Testament covenant
questions.correctAnswer: The Messiah will return only when Israel acknowledges Him as blessed
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:39 prophesies that Israel will not see Jesus again until they say, 'Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord,' linking to Messianic expectation fulfillment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 25 and 26 teach about sanctification and inward purity?
options: True sanctification requires inward cleansing before outward appearances
Outward ritual purity is sufficient for holiness
Inward sin does not affect one's standing with God
questions.correctAnswer: True sanctification requires inward cleansing before outward appearances
questions.explanation: Verses 25 and 26 contrast external cleanliness with internal corruption, teaching that inward purity is essential for true sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment and self-exaltation is taught by combining verses 11 and 12?
options: God exalts the humble and humbles the proud
Exaltation is based on social status
Humility has no bearing on divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: God exalts the humble and humbles the proud
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 teach that greatness in God's kingdom is linked to servanthood and humility, and pride leads to abasement.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about religious leadership and authority is gained from combining verses 8 and 10?
options: Christ alone is the ultimate Master, and believers are brethren without hierarchical titles
Authority is based on human tradition
Calling someone 'father' or 'master' on earth is encouraged
questions.correctAnswer: Christ alone is the ultimate Master, and believers are brethren without hierarchical titles
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 10 emphasize that only Christ is Master, and believers should not seek elevated titles, underscoring equality and Christ's unique authority.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Matthew 23:14 is a later addition and not original. What does Matthew 23:14 actually teach about the scribes and Pharisees?
options: They exploit widows and use prayer as a pretense for gain, facing greater condemnation
They are innocent and blameless in their religious duties
They are praised for their piety and care for widows
They were never criticized by Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: They exploit widows and use prayer as a pretense for gain, facing greater condemnation
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:14 condemns the scribes and Pharisees for devouring widows' houses and making long prayers for pretense, teaching their hypocrisy and coming judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's holiness and the sanctity of sacred objects is taught in Matthew 23:17?
options: The temple sanctifies the gold, showing God's holiness is supreme over material wealth
Gold is greater than the temple and more sacred
Sacred objects have no spiritual significance
Swearing by gold is more binding than by the temple
questions.correctAnswer: The temple sanctifies the gold, showing God's holiness is supreme over material wealth
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:17 calls the Pharisees fools and blind for elevating gold above the temple, teaching the doctrine of God's holiness surpassing material things.

questions.question: What theological truth about the consequences of hypocrisy is expressed in Matthew 23:27-28?
options: Outward righteousness without inward holiness is condemned by God
Hypocrisy is acceptable if the appearance is good
External acts alone justify a person before God
Inward sin is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Outward righteousness without inward holiness is condemned by God
questions.explanation: Verses 27-28 liken the Pharisees to whited sepulchres, beautiful outside but full of dead men's bones inside, condemning superficial righteousness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine justice and the fulfillment of judgment is taught by Matthew 23:35-36?
options: The generation rejecting Christ will bear the cumulative guilt of all righteous blood shed
Judgment is limited to individual sins only
The blood of Abel and Zacharias are unrelated to Israel's culpability
There is no continuity in God's judgment across generations
questions.correctAnswer: The generation rejecting Christ will bear the cumulative guilt of all righteous blood shed
questions.explanation: Verses 35-36 connect the current generation’s rejection to the shedding of righteous blood from Abel to Zacharias, teaching cumulative divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrinal lesson about true greatness and servanthood is taught in Matthew 23:11?
options: Greatness in God's kingdom is demonstrated by serving others
Greatness is measured by social status and power
Leaders should seek honor and recognition
Servanthood is a mark of inferiority
questions.correctAnswer: Greatness in God's kingdom is demonstrated by serving others
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:11 states that the greatest is the servant, teaching that humility and service define true greatness in the kingdom.
